newsitem.title: USA: Sun Micro, USWeb to unveil reseller pact.
newsitem.headline: Sun Micro, USWeb to unveil reseller pact.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc and Internet services firm USWeb Corp Tuesday will launch a strategic reseller accord naming Sun's Netra Internet server family as USWeb's preferred Unix platform, executives said.

Senior executives of both companies said the deal will help USWeb affiliates offer end-to-end corporate Internet and Intranet Web applications in an Internet-based service market expected to grow to billions of dollars in coming years.
Dr. Eric Schmidt, chief technology officer at Sun Microsystems, said his company expects to result in a worldwide deal as USWeb eventually expands overseas.

Sheldon Laube, chief technology officer of USWeb, sited a survey by Mountain View, Calif. market research firm Input that projected that by the end of the year 2000 $20 billion will be spent on Internet-related outsourcing services.

USWeb, which added two affiliates on Monday to bring its total to 25 affiliates in 17 states, was formed in March with $17 million in financing. SOFTBANK Corp's SoftVen unit has a nearly 50 percent stake, on a fully-diluted basis.
USWeb plans to step up its brand campaign in coming weeks as part of the $10 million in marketing expenses it has budgeted for its first 12 months, Laube said.
Schmidt said USWeb offers an entirely new channel for Sun's Netra family, adding significantly to the 95 or so resellers of the products already in place for Sun.

"These guys are going to sell a lot of iron," he said in a telephone interview ahead of the announcement. "They're either the fastest, or closest to the fastest of these new Web entrants in terms of the numbers of customers (they are targetting). It's historic because it's a new channel."
Schmidt said the deal had been done "fairly quickly" in the life of the six-month old startup, adding the deal would benefit both sides in generating order volume.
Sun said it expects the deal to be extended worldwide as USWeb unfolds its strategy of creating a global network of affiliates that offer best-in-class Web services.
"The intent is to go worldwide," said Schmidt. "Our intent is for it to be a worldwide deal."

USWeb Chief Executive Joe Firmage said the company, which is targeting Web projects ranging in size from $10,000 a year to $3 million or so annually, is already setting the stage to enter the Japanese market in the March 1997 quarter.
Firmage noted USWeb has chosen to partner with only slightly more than one percent of its 1,800 applicants.

USWeb aims to garner a significant share of the Web services market by establishing a "first mover" brand name in the market and providing the technological, partnering and operational infrastructure to help a wide range of businesses utilize Web technologies in their businesses.
Schmidt said he sees the Web explosion continuing.

"What we've found out when we talk to our customers is there is no human in the United States, maybe not on the planet, who hasn't read about this and wants to get into it," he said. "You've created...this tremendous demand which is not being full filled...because the stuff is still too hard."
Sun's Netra line is a set of computer products targeted at the Internet market specifically, but USWeb expands sales opportunities to a broader range of customers.
"The Web is a very fast space," said Laube adding that "in next three month, as our national advertising moves out...every business person will know the name USWeb."
